plainLanguage: Of all the shoulder muscles, the chest muscle has some of the best leverage for pulling the upper arm down and across the body.
qualifiers: Moment arm is leverage, not force and not activation: a large moment arm does not by itself establish how much a muscle contributes to a given movement.
Measured by tendon excursion in cadaveric specimens, so it is partially direct for a living lifter.
Leverage varies by sub-region and by joint position, so a single value for the whole muscle is not meaningful.

conditions: glenohumeral horizontal flexion and elevation in the sagittal, scapular and coronal planes

sourceLinks.locator: Abstract, Results (largest depressor and adductor moment arms in pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi and teres major)
Abstract, Results (instantaneous moment arms of 18 sub-regions in eight specimens)
Abstract, Results (internal-rotation leverage dominated by inferior subscapularis)

statement: The pectoralis major is among the muscles with the largest measured adductor moment arms at the glenohumeral joint, alongside the latissimus dorsi and teres major.
